analysis.title: Retail trends to watch: November MTD TRE +0.3%; same-store ShopperTrak traffic -8.2%
key_insights: The GS/TRE Raw Index is +0.3% year over year for November month to date (week 1, ending 11/07). The raw index correlates with monthly same-store sales.
October GS/TRE Raw Index finished at +0.3% year over year. Weekly readings were +0.3% (wk1, 10/10), +0.2% (wk2, 10/17), +0.3% (wk3, 10/24) and +0.5% (wk4, 10/31).
ShopperTrak same-store retail traffic was -8.2% year over year for the week ending 11/07/26. Same-store outlet mall traffic was -12.5%.

Goldman notes the correlation between ShopperTrak year-over-year changes and its comp sales indices is low, partly because shopper visits do not reflect changes in conversion trends. Directional changes in visits have some relationship with comp sales of apparel retailers and department stores over time.
US average gasoline price was $4.00 per gallon as of Nov 9, 2026, down 4% week on week and month to date but up 31% year on year. West Coast was highest at $5.11 and Gulf Coast lowest at $3.48.
National average temperature was 58.2 degrees, 6.2 degrees above normal and 4.4 above last year, per the shopper's barometer weather table.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The raw index tracks monthly same-store sales. Readings near +0.3% are consistent with modest positive comps. October was also +0.3%.
October finished at +0.3% against -0.1% in the same month of 2025.
Store visits fell sharply year over year. Goldman says visits correlate only weakly with comp sales.

macro_indicators.indicator: ShopperTrak same-store outlet mall traffic, YoY
macro_indicators.interpretation: Outlet mall visits fell more than broader retail traffic.

macro_indicators.reading: $4.00 per gallon, -4% week on week, +31% year on year
macro_indicators.interpretation: Gasoline is sharply higher than a year ago, though it eased over the past week.

risk_factors: Weak ShopperTrak traffic (-8.2% same-store retail) contrasts with a positive raw sales index, and Goldman notes visits do not capture conversion changes.
Gasoline prices are up 31% year on year, which could weigh on consumer spending.
